long_biography.plain_text:
Engineering rather than finance shaped Will Apold's first business career. After studying mechanical and fisheries engineering at Dalhousie University, he became a fishing-industry consultant and plant manager. He then spent twenty-five years as president of TAVEL, an engineering-design company specializing in aquaculture, food processing, automation and software. The work joined process engineering with practical production systems for industrial clients.

The same design discipline carried into renewable power. Through Natural Forces Technologies, Apold invested in wind projects and led a company that co-developed and retained interests in operating wind farms. Dragon Glass Capital broadened this activity into a portfolio spanning renewable energy, industrial technologies and software. Product-development consulting kept technical design part of his work.
